permission.description: An opaque handle of the form permref:<provider>:<name> plus a scope set drawn from a closed vocabulary (read, write, append, delete, execute). Admin is refused outright, an unknown scope is refused, and an empty or duplicated scope set is refused. There is no wildcard.
permission.claim_boundary: A declared scope is a request, not an enforcement point. Enforcement remains DEFERRED-EXTERNAL.

purpose.description: Why the permission is needed, in plain words. A missing purpose, a vague purpose such as 'anything' or 'unspecified', markup, and an over-long purpose are all refused.
purpose.claim_boundary: The purpose is recorded and shown to the user. The host does not judge whether a stated purpose is true.

data_categories.description: The data categories the grant may reach, from a closed vocabulary (account_identity, workspace_metadata, novel_content, character_content, usage_metrics, billing_metadata, secret_metadata). An empty set, an unknown category, and a duplicated category are refused.
data_categories.claim_boundary: Categories are declared, not resolved. The brokered read path is step 119.23.

destination.description: The host the grant sends data to, plus a destination kind (local, first_party, third_party). A plaintext http destination is refused, a malformed host is refused, and a third-party destination without explicit cross-organisation consent is refused.
destination.claim_boundary: The destination is declared by the requester. This contract performs no network resolution and no connectivity check.

duration.description: The bounded lifetime of the grant (session, 1h, 1d, 7d, 30d, 90d). An unknown duration is refused, and a mutating scope may not be granted until revoked: a write, append, or delete grant must carry a wall-clock end.
duration.claim_boundary: Expiry is evaluated against the caller-supplied clock. The contract does not schedule a timer or run a background sweep.

revocation.description: How the grant is taken back: an opaque revokeref handle, an immediate flag that must be true, and a grace window of at most five minutes. Revocation is always possible, from any state, and is idempotent.
revocation.claim_boundary: Revocation is recorded in this process. Cross-process revocation propagation remains DEFERRED-EXTERNAL.

least_privilege.description: An attestation that the requested scope is the smallest that works: a plain justification, an explicit minimal-scope flag that must be true, and the review date. A grant that is not attested is refused.
least_privilege.claim_boundary: Least privilege is attested by the requester and checked structurally. The host cannot verify that the requested scope is truly minimal.

acceptance.default_posture: deny-by-default: state none is not usable
acceptance.consent_lifecycle: request, grant, deny, revoke; a grant requires a prior request; a re-grant after revoke or deny requires a new request
acceptance.fail_safe: revocation is always possible from any state and is idempotent
